commands.short: Create the worktree and tab, start an agent and send it the prompt
commands.long:
tkt start creates or reuses the ticket's worktree through worktrunk, opens a
herdr tab named after the ticket, starts an agent in build mode (Claude Code
with --dangerously-skip-permissions, OpenCode on its Build agent) and sends it
the prompt, typically the dispatcher's start-ticket block.

Without an ID, tkt start takes the first ticket id in the prompt; with both,
they must match. Without a prompt, it sends the start stage line. --prompt -
reads the prompt from stdin, which keeps a long prompt out of your shell
history; --prompt-file reads it from a file.

The prompt's Model: line, when it has one, picks the preset (tkt help config);
--as picks one yourself.

tkt start refuses when an agent already runs in the worktree: use tkt run for
a fresh session, or tkt resume to bring back the last one. When the agent stops
at a startup dialog, answer it in the tab and rerun the same tkt start: it
continues where it stopped.
commands.example:
xclip -selection clipboard -o | tkt start --prompt -
  tkt start ACM-12
  tkt start ACM-12 --prompt-file plan-request.md --as fast
  tkt start ACM-12 --dry-run

commands.short: Replace the ticket's idle agent with a fresh session and send a stage line
commands.long:
tkt run closes the ticket's idle agent and starts a fresh session in the same
pane, on the ticket's preset, then sends the stage's line. The new agent
remembers nothing of the old conversation and does not need to: every stage
reads what it needs from the branch, the pull request and the tracker. Use it
to begin the next stage with a clean context.

Stages:
  review   review-pr reviews the pull request at its head and posts a verdict.
           Run it when the agent ends with Status: READY_FOR_REVIEW.
  address  address-pr-review fixes the valid findings, answers the rest and
           pushes. Run it when the review asks for changes, you left comments,
           or the merge stopped with Status: HUMAN_QA_FAILED.
  sync     address-pr-review merges the base into the branch. Run it on
           Status: BLOCKED_FOR_SYNC, or when the pull request conflicts.
  ci       finds why the checks fail at the head, fixes it and pushes once.
  verify   runs the pull request's human verification steps in a browser and
           reports each one. It changes no code and posts nothing.
  start    runs start-ticket again and returns a new plan.

config.toml can change these lines or add stages (tkt help config).

tkt run refuses while the agent works or waits for your answer (tkt wait
blocks until it is done). It also refuses while the ticket is still in
planning, because that agent may hold a plan waiting for your approval;
approve it in the tab instead. --force replaces it anyway, and also replaces
an agent in a state tkt does not recognize.
commands.example:
tkt run ACM-12 review
  tkt run ACM-12 review --as big
  tkt run ACM-12 address
  tkt run ACM-12 --prompt "Check the flaky login test again."

commands.short: Relaunch the ticket's newest session when no agent runs for it
commands.long:
tkt resume brings back the ticket's last conversation when no agent runs for
it: you closed the tab, the agent exited or crashed, herdr restarted, or the
machine rebooted. It relaunches the newest session (the one tkt recorded,
otherwise the newest Claude Code or OpenCode session in the worktree) in
bypass mode, in the ticket's tab or a new one, and sends nothing, so the agent
waits where it stopped.

Use it instead of tkt run when the conversation matters, such as a plan
waiting for approval. When an agent already runs, tkt resume says where and
changes nothing; --focus switches to its tab.
commands.example:
tkt resume ACM-12
  tkt resume ACM-12 --focus
  tkt resume ACM-12 --session 22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222

commands.short: List ticket worktrees with their state and the next step
commands.long:
tkt ls lists every ticket worktree, or the tickets given, with its tab, agent
state, the last Status: line on the agent's screen, pull request, checks,
review verdict at the head, commits behind the base, and the next step.

The next step is the first of these rules that matches:
  1. The pull request is merged: tkt done ID.
  2. The agent works: wait (tkt wait ID); or it waits for an answer: answer it.
  3. No pull request yet: tkt resume ID when no agent runs; otherwise approve
     the plan, read the agent's reason, or check the agent in its tab.
  4. The checks are pending: wait for CI.
  5. The review says the base moved, or the pull request conflicts: tkt run ID sync.
  6. The review at the head has findings: tkt run ID address.
  7. The checks fail: tkt run ID ci.
  8. The review at the head is clear: tkt run ID verify.
  9. Anything else: wait for review, or tkt run ID review when no automated
     reviewer runs on the forge.

A verdict on an older head does not count, so after every push the next step
waits for a new review. With --json each row's next step is an object whose
argv, when set, is the command to run. tkt ls reads pull requests through gh,
so outside GitHub forges those columns show ?.
commands.example:
tkt ls
  tkt ls ACM-12 --json
  tkt ls --json | jq -r '.result.rows[] | select(.next.kind == "command") | .next.text'

flags.name: no-fetch
flags.usage: skip the git fetch that refreshes the commits-behind count

commands.short: Block until the ticket's agent needs you or has finished
commands.long:
tkt wait blocks until the ticket's agent is idle, blocked or done, that is,
until it has finished or needs you, then prints its state and the last
Status: line on its screen. --until picks other states.

A program that drives tkt waits with it instead of polling tkt ls. With
--timeout, a wait that runs out ends with exit 4 and the code wait_timeout.
commands.example:
tkt wait ACM-12
  tkt wait ACM-12 --timeout 30m --json
  tkt wait ACM-12 --until blocked

flags.name: pane
flags.usage: wait for the agent in PANE when several run in the worktree

flags.name: timeout
flags.usage: give up after DURATION, such as 30m (default: wait without limit)

flags.name: until
flags.usage: stop at STATE: idle, working, blocked or done; repeat it or separate with commas (default idle, blocked, done)

commands.short: Check the tools, versions and configuration tkt needs
commands.long:
tkt doctor checks what the other commands need and reports each check as ok,
warn, fail or skip: git, worktrunk and herdr at their minimum versions, the
herdr pane, gh when the forge is GitHub, the harness of every preset, the
project's lifecycle configuration, config.toml, worktrunk's hooks and the log
directory. It exits 3 when a check fails.

On a terminal it groups the checks, colors them and ends with a summary.
Otherwise, and with --json, it prints the plain format that programs read.

commands.short: Describe every command, flag, result and error code as JSON
commands.long:
tkt schema prints a JSON description of tkt for programs that drive it: every
command with its arguments, flags and result fields, the exit statuses and
error codes, and the environment variables tkt reads. It is built from the same
definitions as the help, so the two always agree.

Without --json it prints the description itself; with --json it is the result
of the usual envelope.
commands.example:
tkt schema
  tkt schema --json | jq '.result.errors[] | select(.exit == 4) | .code'

commands.short: Replace tkt with the latest release, or with VERSION
commands.long:
tkt update replaces the running tkt with the latest full release from
git.rogs.me, or with the release VERSION names. It downloads the binary for
this system and the release's SHA256SUMS, checks the checksum, runs the new
binary once with --version, and only then renames it over the old one. If a
step fails, the old binary stays. The checksum catches a broken download, not
a compromised host.

Without VERSION, tkt update does nothing when tkt is already at the latest
release or newer. The latest release skips prereleases; name one, such as
v0.3.0-rc.1, to install it. A named VERSION also installs an older release.

A development build, whose tkt --version prints dev, has no version to
compare, so tkt update replaces it only with --force. A go build inside a git
checkout prints a version such as v0.2.1-0.20261019212235-569e7a5572c4, which
counts as newer than v0.2.0. --check reports what tkt update would do and
changes nothing. When tkt runs through a symlink, tkt update
replaces the file the link points to.
commands.example:
tkt update
  tkt update --check
  tkt update v0.3.0-rc.1

flags.name: check
flags.usage: report whether a release would replace tkt, and change nothing

flags.name: force
flags.usage: replace a development build, or reinstall the same version

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(tkt completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	tkt completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/tkt

#### macOS:

	tkt completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/tkt

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

flags.name: no-descriptions
flags.usage: disable completion descriptions

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(tkt completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	tkt completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_tkt"

#### macOS:

	tkt completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_tkt

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

flags.name: no-descriptions
flags.usage: disable completion descriptions

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for fish
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	tkt completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	tkt completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/tkt.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

flags.name: no-descriptions
flags.usage: disable completion descriptions

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	tkt completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

environment.description: the pane tkt runs in; tkt never starts an agent in it
